purpose: Replace editorial-placement wording in the newly created profiles with factual philosophical introductions; preserve previous input.

people.name: Plato
people.expected_before: A philosopher whose dialogues investigate justice, knowledge and the examined life. The dramatic Socrates in these works is not simply interchangeable with Plato.
people.biography: A philosopher whose dialogues investigate justice, knowledge and the examined life. The dramatic Socrates in these works is not simply interchangeable with Plato.

people.name: Aristotle
people.expected_before: Breadth across disciplines supports leading historical consideration. Influence does not certify current scientific correctness.
people.biography: A philosopher whose surviving works range across logic, biology, metaphysics and ethics. Much of this corpus uses compressed technical prose and has a complex editorial history.

people.name: Immanuel Kant
people.expected_before: Several reception routes support a leading position. Exact position against non-European traditions is unresolved.
people.biography: A philosopher whose three Critiques connect knowledge, ethics and judgment through questions of reason and autonomy.

people.name: Confucius
people.expected_before: Long reception supports a high historical case. Received text and historical person need separation.
people.biography: A thinker associated with ritual, virtue and the relations between family and political life. The Analects preserves multiple representations of him through later transmission.

people.name: David Hume
people.expected_before: Scholarly and comparative selections support high standing. Contemporary historical fame differs from later philosophical fame.
people.biography: A philosopher and historian who investigated experience, causal reasoning and human nature. His Enquiries revisit subjects of the earlier Treatise with both continuity and revision.

people.name: Avicenna / Ibn Sīnā
people.expected_before: Cross-disciplinary and interreligious reception supports a high place. Medicine and philosophy contribute different kinds of influence.
people.biography: A philosopher and physician whose work connects scientific and philosophical inquiry. Later thinkers across religious communities developed, revised and challenged his arguments.

people.name: Nāgārjuna
people.expected_before: Buddhist reception across Asia supports high historical consideration. Work attributions are not uniformly secure.
people.biography: A Buddhist philosopher associated with arguments about emptiness and the absence of intrinsic nature. Not every work later attributed to him has secure authorship.

people.name: Thomas Aquinas
people.expected_before: Scholastic reception supports upper-group consideration. A comparative worldwide rank needs more than reference coverage.
people.biography: A philosopher and theologian who systematically reworked Aristotelian thought. His theological syntheses and disputed questions contain extensive philosophical argument.

people.name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
people.expected_before: Language and method provide a strong historical case. Do not flatten contested phases into two simple doctrines.
people.biography: A philosopher concerned with language and the practice of philosophy. The relationship between the Tractatus and Philosophical Investigations remains a subject of interpretation.

people.name: Śaṅkara
people.expected_before: Vedānta reception supports an upper historical group. Religious authority and philosophical argument need separate evaluation.
people.biography: An Advaita philosopher whose commentaries explore consciousness, metaphysics and methods of teaching, including readings of the Brahmasutras, Bhagavad Gita and principal Upanishads.

people.name: Baruch Spinoza
people.expected_before: Critical, editorial and reader evidence support inclusion. Reader enthusiasm is self-selected.
people.biography: A philosopher linking metaphysics with the passions, freedom, happiness and political life. His works include the Ethics and Theological-Political Treatise.

people.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
people.expected_before: Psychological and value critique supports high standing. Authored works must be separated from notebook compilations.
people.biography: A philosopher whose writing joins psychological criticism with a re-examination of values. His authored books must be distinguished from posthumous notebook compilations.

people.name: Simone de Beauvoir
people.expected_before: Independent contribution merits more than derivative status. Do not reduce the corpus to one book.
people.biography: A writer and philosopher whose contributions span existentialism, ethics and feminism, across theory, fiction and memoir.

people.name: al-Ghazālī
people.expected_before: Philosophical criticism and later reception support inclusion. Reject unsupported philosophy-decline shorthand.
people.biography: A thinker whose criticism of selected philosophical doctrines coexists with the use of philosophical argument in theology. His work resists a simple description as rejection of philosophy.

people.name: Mencius
people.expected_before: Comparative ethics supports substantial historical consideration. Text compilation is distinct from personal authorship.
people.biography: A thinker associated with ethical cultivation and debates about human nature. The received Mengzi was compiled by followers and subsequently edited.

people.name: Hannah Arendt
people.expected_before: Public and scholarly reception supports inclusion. Different books and controversies require separate treatment.
people.biography: A political thinker whose books investigate totalitarianism, human activity and judgment. Her distinct arguments and public controversies should be read in their particular contexts.

people.name: John Rawls
people.expected_before: Institutional and international reception support inclusion. National reception produces conflicting political interpretations.
people.biography: A political philosopher whose theory of justice generated extensive international debate. Its reception has taken different forms within different political and academic institutions.

people.name: Frantz Fanon
people.expected_before: Africana and postcolonial reception sustain the historical case. Further independent debate over violence remains needed.
people.biography: A thinker whose work examines racism, alienation and colonial liberation. His books develop different perspectives on lived experience and political transformation.

people.name: Mozi
people.expected_before: A thinker associated with the Mohist tradition. The received text also reflects later members of the school, so the collective corpus is not treated as single-person authorship.
people.biography: A thinker associated with the Mohist tradition. The received text also reflects later members of the school, so the collective corpus is not treated as single-person authorship.

people.name: John Stuart Mill
people.expected_before: Canonical argument supports historical inclusion. Colonial exclusions complicate a universalist reading.
people.biography: A philosopher who defended open discussion and individuality through arguments about fallibility and utility. His account of liberty also contains exclusions that require critical attention.

people.name: B. R. Ambedkar
people.expected_before: Indian political reception supports a substantial case. A book-level comparison does not measure the whole philosopher.
people.biography: An anti-caste thinker whose work links social hierarchy with questions of democratic transformation and recognition.

people.name: Mary Wollstonecraft
people.expected_before: Feminist philosophical reception supports consideration. More work-specific and comparative evidence needed.
people.biography: A writer and philosopher whose critique of women’s condition connects education and rights with wider social relations. Her work also extends into travel writing.

people.name: Mullā Ṣadrā
people.expected_before: Later Islamic philosophy challenges a truncated historical canon. English availability must be verified for a particular entry work.
people.biography: A philosopher whose thought brings rational argument into conversation with revelation and mystical insight. His major works include the Four Journeys.
